description: Find every figure written with a given number of decimals in a document on this machine: the value, the characters as printed, and the row and column they sit in, numbered as read_table numbers them. Two decimals is how a page tells a sum of money from a reference number without knowing what money is; ask for 0 decimals to take every number. The answer opens with the verdict of the reading, reliable, doubtful or unreadable, and reliable only means nothing looked wrong. What a figure MEANS - a debit, a balance, a date written as digits - is not read here: that is the reading, and check_citations is how a claim about it is checked. The file is read on this machine and never uploaded.

decimals.description: Exactly how many decimals a figure must be written with. Defaults to 2. 0 takes every number, reference numbers included.

from.description: First row to look in, 1 for the start. Rows keep the numbers read_table gave them.

limit.description: Rows to look in, at most 2000. Defaults to 200. What is left is counted and named, never silently dropped.

maximumPages.description: How many pages to open. Defaults to 40, which bounds a runaway read rather than describing your document: raise it for an annual report.

path.description: Absolute path to the file on this machine. It is read here and never uploaded.

name: find_amounts

row.description: The row, numbered as read_table numbers it: cite it in check_citations.

written.description: The characters the page printed, untouched.

reason.description: Why the file did not open, when the library could tell: empty, too-big, no-text, too-slow, or the kind of bytes it was. Only on an unreadable verdict.

title: Find the figures a document prints, with the row to cite
